transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m the one making a problem, but I’m not. My family and some of my friends keep saying, “Look at the bank papers, nothing was taken,” like that settles it, but it doesn’t. Papers can be made to look a certain way, or things can be moved around, and I know what I know.

This has been going on for over a year now. They’ve been hiding my money, and then they cover it up with all these excuses — bills that suddenly need paying, fundraisers that don’t make sense, trip plans where the numbers don’t add up. It’s like every time I ask straight out, there’s another story ready. And then they all look at me like I’m being difficult for confronting them.

I came because they keep telling me to stop bringing it up, but how can I stop when nobody will just tell the truth? I keep having to ask them and confront them because if I don’t, they’ll just keep pretending nothing happened.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds, or seen things, that other people around you couldn't hear or see?

No, not like that. I mean, I hear regular things — people talking, the TV, stuff outside — but I don’t hear voices talking to me when nobody’s there or anything like that. And I don’t think I’ve seen things other people couldn’t see.

Sometimes people make it sound like I’m “seeing things” just because I notice what’s going on, but that’s different. I’m not seeing ghosts or shapes or people who aren’t there. I’m talking about real things that happen and what people say and do. So, no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had that.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, such as forgetting recent conversations, misplacing things more often, or having trouble concentrating?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I forget little normal things sometimes, like anybody does, but I haven’t noticed some big change where I can’t remember conversations or I’m lost all the time or anything like that.

Sometimes if I’m upset or if a lot is going on, I might have to stop and think, “Wait, what was I just about to do?” but that feels normal to me. I can follow what people are saying. I remember what was talked about. I don’t think my memory is the problem. If that’s what you mean, no, I haven’t really noticed a recent change like that.

Aside from this situation with your family and money, would you say you generally have a hard time trusting other people in your life—like coworkers, doctors, or friends—even in situations that have nothing to do with your finances?

I don’t know… I mean, I wouldn’t say I just don’t trust everybody for no reason, if that’s what you mean. Like, if someone is just doing their job or I meet somebody somewhere, I’m not automatically thinking something about them. I can talk to people. I can be normal with people.

But I do pay attention, you know? I think anybody would, especially after people close to you start acting a certain way. So with doctors or people asking questions, yeah, I might wonder why they’re asking it or what they’re going to do with what I say. That’s not me being against everyone, that’s just being careful. Same with friends—if they’re not involved in this, then I don’t have a big issue with them. But if they start repeating the same things my family says, then of course I’m going to question it.

So… generally? No, I don’t think I have a hard time trusting everyone. It’s more when something doesn’t add up, or when people act like I’m supposed to ignore what I already know. Then I’m not going to just smile and pretend.
Outside of this situation with your family, how have things been going for you generally—are you still able to keep up with work, hobbies, and spending time with people the way you used to?

Mostly, yes. I mean, besides the fighting and stress about the money with my family, I still do my regular things. I make my own food, I keep track of what I need to do, I get myself to the county clinic when I’m supposed to go, and I go to my assistance appointments. I’m not just sitting around unable to handle anything.

I keep my things in order, too. Maybe not fancy or anything, but the same way I always have. I know where my papers are, I know what appointments I have, I take care of my own meals. It’s really that money situation that causes the arguments and makes everything harder. Outside of that, I’m still managing my day-to-day stuff.
